name: Fireworks AI On-Demand deployments (per GPU-second)
region: primary regions plus region-restricted deployments at a 1.5x premium
price_basis: per GPU-hour, 'Pay per GPU second, with no extra charges for start-up times'. H100 80GB $0.134/min = $8.00/h; H200 141GB $0.134/min = $8.00/h; B200 180GB $0.217/min = $13.00/h; B300 288GB $0.250/min = $15.00/h; GB300 $0.334/min = $20.00/h. Fetched 2026-10-03.
notes: Fireworks is INFERENCE-SHAPED, and the price reflects it: at $8.00/H100-hour this is the second most expensive on-demand H100 in the slice, above AWS p5's $6.88 and far above Runpod's $3.49, and you get a dedicated deployment with their inference runtime rather than a bare GPU. That is a deliberate trade, not a mistake - compare it to Runpod serverless H100 ($4.79 per worker-hour) or CoreWeave's inference-platform H100 ($6.16, but gated to that platform) and the picture is that Fireworks is priced as a product, not as silicon. Two real details. (1) The published minute and hour columns are internally inconsistent - $0.134 x 60 = $8.04, printed as $8.00 - so treat the hourly figure as a rounded convenience and the per-minute figure as the one that is actually charged. (2) Region-restricted deployments are a stated 1.5x premium, which on H100 is $12.00/hour and would put a data-residency requirement above every hyperscaler in this slice. Fireworks also publishes per-token serverless and per-token training prices on the same page; those are a different unit and are deliberately not recorded as supply. Their per-second billing with no start-up charge is the genuinely useful engineering property here.
